game_title: Examination practice · C Scope Circuit · Compare local and global · variation 5
game_concept: A tower defense set in Sand Dunes – Merchant Waystation, a waystation for merchants: the scarab scholar must handle giant scorpions while practicing debugging & combined skills. Core idea – Code Reading Relay: Read short programs as a relay and predict their output line by line.
theme: Sand Dunes – Merchant Waystation: a waystation for merchants
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
secondary_mechanics: Bonus coins for fast correct moves
player_objective: Week 8 examination practice: Build 3 parallel branches, merge every branch by SUM, and feed the merged signal back for 3 passes before the output probe. In the scope controller, initialize a local from visible global state. Print the scope trace [9, 8], then send the incoming signal with writeOutput(signal) into the broadcast splitter. Final file-scope values: {'steps': 8}. Pass all 3 signal tests.
controls: Drag components and connect pins. A splitter broadcasts a copy to every branch; the SUM merger waits for one result from each branch in the same pass. LOOP sends intermediate results back to split, and the final result to output. Select Program node to edit each C controller. Run tests every case; Step highlights the active node, wire and C line. Each node invocation starts fresh C scopes. Feedback passes and execution are bounded. readInput and writeOutput are bounded LogiCade helpers from logicade.h, not standard C functions.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
learning_alignment: CP1 Week 8: Compare local and global
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Code Reading Relay' (Week 9 slot 10), mission type 'Survival Siege', and setting 'Merchant Waystation'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.

tutorial: Read the C scope mission and expected signal traces.

Write file-scope declarations before main and local declarations inside their blocks.

Use Program node to edit every branch. Step inspects scopes and signals; Run verifies all tests.
source_player_objective: Protect the sundial from giant scorpions in Merchant Waystation: keep the predicted meter above zero by applying the concept correctly until the 38-second timer ends.
source_lose_condition: predicted drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 38-second timer ends.

hint: Wire every splitter branch into the SUM merger. The feedback controller repeats the merged signal for the required pass count, then sends it to the probe. Declare globals before main. Braces create local scopes; an inner declaration hides an outer name until its block ends. Use Step to inspect the variable scopes and output trace.
